divergences.old: jwt decode - failing with "Invalid JWT: expected 3 dot-separated parts"
divergences.toil: - reads the token from stdin on the CLI, dropping one trailing line ending (echo $TOKEN | toil util jwt decode -), so the token stays out of the process list and shell history. Over MCP, - is INVALID_INPUT, since stdin is the protocol there
divergences.why: A JWT is a credential, and argv is visible to every process on the machine; stdin is how toil takes one.

divergences.old: jwt decode accepting a header or payload that is JSON but not an object, so bnVsbA.bnVsbA.x comes back as { header: null, payload: null } and WzEsMl0.e30.x as a header of [1, 2] (#75 item 1)
divergences.toil: A header or payload that decodes to null, a boolean, a number, a string or an array is INVALID_INPUT: "Invalid JWT: header is not a JSON object", or the same for the payload. A JSON object decodes as before
divergences.why: RFC 7519 section 7.2 says to reject a JWT whose JOSE header or claims set is not a JSON object. A local run of decodeJwt on those tokens confirmed the old result (#75 item 1).

divergences.old: jwt decode handing each segment to Node's base64 decoder, which skips characters outside the alphabet, accepts standard base64 + and /, and drops a leftover character when the length is 1 mod 4, so a damaged header such as eyJh!!bGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9 still decodes to {"alg":"HS256"}. The signature segment was returned as whatever text it was, including one with a newline in it (#75 item 2)
divergences.toil: The header, payload and signature must be base64url: letters, digits, - and _, with = only as one or two padding characters at the end, and a length that can be whole bytes. Anything else is INVALID_INPUT: "Invalid JWT: header is not valid base64url", or the same for the payload or the signature. Whitespace in a segment is rejected, not skipped. An empty signature is valid base64url and is still accepted, which is how alg none is written. A signature that passes is returned as the text it is: it is not decoded and not verified
divergences.why: RFC 7515 section 2 and appendix C, and RFC 4648 section 3.3, require the base64url alphabet and say to reject anything outside it. A skipped character hides a damaged token. Trailing = stays accepted because that appendix allows padding. The signature is the third segment of the same encoding, so it gets the same alphabet check. Checked locally (#75 item 2).

divergences.old: jwt decode turning bytes that are not UTF-8 into U+FFFD, so a payload whose bytes are {"a":"<0xff>"} (segment eyJhIjoi_yJ9) decodes to { "a": "\uFFFD" } (#75 item 3)
divergences.toil: A header or payload that is not valid UTF-8 is INVALID_INPUT: "Invalid JWT: header is not valid UTF-8", or the same for the payload. Valid UTF-8, including a real U+FFFD character, still decodes
divergences.why: RFC 7519 section 7.2 requires the header and claims set to be UTF-8. The bytes a signature covers are the ones in the segment, and a replacement character would show a different claim. Checked locally (#75 item 3).

divergences.old: jwt decode reporting a Bearer prefix as "Invalid JWT: header is not valid JSON", keeping a trailing newline in data.signature, and accepting a leading space because the base64 decoder skipped it (#75 item 4)
divergences.toil: The token is still refused. A prefix is not stripped and surrounding whitespace is not trimmed. A token that starts with "Bearer " (any case) is INVALID_INPUT: "Invalid JWT: remove the 'Bearer ' prefix". One with leading or trailing whitespace is INVALID_INPUT: "Invalid JWT: token has surrounding whitespace". Neither message repeats the token. jwt decode - still drops one trailing line ending before that check
divergences.why: RFC 7519 section 7.2 says to reject extra characters. The issue's other fix is an error that names the prefix, so a paste from an Authorization header is not reported as a bad header. Checked locally (#75 item 4, partly confirmed).
